title: Gel Electrophoresis Apparatus (Chamber & Power Supply)

references.label: General molecular biology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Separates nucleic acid or protein molecules by size (and, for proteins run under denaturing conditions, largely by size alone) as they migrate through a gel matrix under an applied electric field, most commonly used with agarose gels for DNA/RNA fragments.
operatingPrinciple: The negatively charged phosphate backbone of nucleic acids (or an SDS coating applied to proteins in SDS-PAGE) causes molecules to migrate toward the positive electrode when a voltage is applied across the gel; the gel matrix acts as a molecular sieve, so smaller molecules move through it faster than larger ones, separating a mixed sample into size-based bands over time.
basicOperation: Prepare and cast the gel (e.g. agarose in an appropriate buffer) in the casting tray with a comb to form sample wells, and allow it to solidify.
Place the solidified gel in the chamber, submerged in running buffer matching the gel's buffer system.
Load samples (mixed with loading dye) into the wells, including a molecular weight ladder in at least one lane.
Close the lid, confirm correct electrode polarity (samples should migrate toward the positive electrode, away from the wells), and run at the appropriate voltage/time for the gel and application.
Stop the run before dye front or bands of interest run off the gel, then visualize (e.g. under UV/blue light for a stained agarose gel).
importantSettings: Applied voltage and run time (higher voltage speeds migration but can increase band smearing/heat)
Buffer system matching the gel type
maintenance: Rinse the chamber and casting tray after use to prevent buffer salt crystallization and residual stain buildup.
Inspect electrode leads and lid interlock for damage periodically.

commonErrors.problem: Bands run in the wrong direction or do not migrate
commonErrors.cause: Electrodes reversed, or buffer level too low to complete the circuit
commonErrors.fix: Confirm correct polarity before starting and ensure the gel is fully submerged in running buffer

commonErrors.cause: Voltage too high for the run, overloaded wells, or degraded/impure sample
commonErrors.fix: Reduce voltage, load an appropriate sample amount, and check sample quality

safety: Never open the lid or reach into the chamber while the power supply is running — this is a genuine electrical shock hazard.
If using ethidium bromide or another intercalating stain, handle and dispose of it per the facility's chemical/mutagen safety procedures.
Use appropriate UV-eye protection if visualizing stained gels under a UV transilluminator.
